newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor studies buying Brazilian firm - paper.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor studies buying Brazilian firm - paper.

text.p: Portuguese cement firm Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal is studying a possible purchase of Brazilian cement producer Companhia de Materiais Sulfurosos - Matisulfur, a Lisbon newspaper reported.
Diario Economico quoted unidentified officials involved in the process as saying any deal would only take place after the privatisation of up to 45 percent of Cimpor, due next month.
The paper quoted a Brazilian press report as saying Matisulfur, located in Grande Belo Horizonte, was valued at some $100 million and had a productive capacity of one million tonnes of cement.
Cimpor officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
A company source told Reuters last month that Cimpor had potential to invest up to 250 billion escudos ($1.6 billion) in foreign acquisitions up to the year 2001.
Cimpor was considering South America, Spain, northern and southern Africa as potential areas to acquire cement manufacturers, the source said.
Last month Cimpor bought Moroccan cement firm Asment Temara for 11.8 billion escudos ($76 million).

Diario Economico quoted one official as saying: "Brazil is a priority market for Cimpor, due to its cultural similarities (to Portugal), its high growth potential and low level of concentration, but there are other possibilities in Chile and Argentina."
